offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. diagnosis.hypothesis: payments-api was redeployed at 21:06:15Z with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. Our records store amounts in cents, so each charge sent to the provider since then is 100 times too large. pmt_000247 ($38.63) was charged $3,863.00, and every later payment shows the same pattern. Because our payments table holds the correct cents amount while the provider holds 100x, payments_match_provider fails. The findings rose from 49 at the alert to 59 at c1, so the damage is still growing. matches_provider passes because the ledger books the provider's webhook amounts; our payment rows are what disagree. One payment, pmt_000252, is still pending on our side although the provider charged it, likely a race with the check. Open questions: the deploy log entry does not show the setting's value before the deploy (presumably cents), and I did not see the request body to confirm the amount sent on the wire.
